sentence: This project evaluates a community-based intervention that tries to improve access to prostate cancer screening and support informed decision-making.
This project engineers immune cells called macrophages to engulf pathogenic protein and disrupt inflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how faulty forms of fused in sarcoma disrupt transport between the nucleus and cytoplasm in human neurons.
This project builds AI tools and data that help rehabilitation researchers diagnose, monitor, and improve outcomes for people with conditions that limit mobility.
This project studies how oxytocin eases pain through circuits in the spinal cord, and how massage may help it work in mice.
This project tests whether cornea-like organoids grown from reprogrammed somatic cells can supply cells and tissue for treating corneal injury and scarring.
This project builds a test that uses machine learning on 3D pathology datasets of biopsies to judge the risk of Barrett's esophagus.
This project studies which genes and molecular pathways control the shape and size of organs and tissue growth in multicellular organisms.
This project tests a cell-free way to regenerate bladder tissue using a scaffold and a non-human primate model.
This project works with primary care teams to build and pilot a team-based care model that increases cervical cancer screening in low-resource primary care settings.
This project makes cell lines and human brain cells to study how gene variants change the risk of Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds AI tools that spot communication and teamwork failures during cardiac surgery and give feedback to surgical teams.
This project studies how low oxygen in non-small cell lung cancer tumors shields them from the immune system and causes treatment resistance.
This project studies how environmental pollutants harm mitochondria and how genetic differences change the response to that harm.
This project develops a brain imaging tool that shows where noradrenaline acts in the brain, for use in posttraumatic stress disorder.
This project studies transplantation biology and cellular therapy for leukemia and lymphoma using preclinical models and clinical trials.
This project studies how single neurons combine sensory signals with cognitive inputs, using experiments and computer models.
This project studies how receptor cells in the inner ear turn a sound-induced mechanical stimulus into an electrical signal.
This project studies how mRNA is regulated during presynaptic assembly in a living nematode, using live imaging and biochemical methods.
This project studies how the tumor microenvironment affects immune cells, and tests ways to overcome immune suppression in cancer.
